topPRs.title: validation: Add sepolia standard versions for op-contracts/v8.0.0-rc.2
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Adds the `["op-contracts/v8.0.0-rc.2"]` entry to `standard-versions-sepolia.toml` for the U20 release candidate ([op-contracts/v8.0.0-rc.2](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/releases/tag/op-contracts%2Fv8.0.0-rc.2), commit `7799a24`).

Sepolia only. The mainnet entry follows once the implementations are deployed there.

## Source of the values

Addresses come from the `op-deployer bootstrap implementations` output (`just deploy-opcm` at the tag). Every recorded address was checked against Sepolia: `version()` on each address equals the version in this entry and equals the `@custom:semver` in the tagged source.

Changed since v7.0.0-rc.4:

| Contract | Version | Address |
| --- | --- | --- |
| system_config | 3.14.2 -> 4.0.0 | `0x670b850a235a6fa98cd7a195eb139d0277e471fa` |
| optimism_portal | 5.6.1 -> 5.8.0 | `0x1005217ad392dc64cef501fa1777a27d42166748` |
| superchain_config | 2.4.2 -> 2.4.3 | `0x5570b1f2b97b1e35b5c6f9ee76f6cf02c9917504` |
| op_contracts_manager | 7.1.17 -> 8.0.0 | `0xda83150fd745d35bb347a7afaf2d7af1d1e8b2b6` |

All other contracts have unchanged bytecode, so CREATE2 returned the same addresses as v7.0.0-rc.4. `fault_dispute_game` (2.4.2) and `permissioned_dispute_game` (2.4.0) stay version-only, as in earlier entries.

## Two things to note

1. `protocol_versions` is absent. `ProtocolVersions.sol` was removed from the monorepo (ethereum-optimism/optimism#20527), so the release no longer deploys it. This is the first entry without that key.
2. The deploy output also contains addresses with no field in `validation.VersionConfig`, so they are not recorded here: `superFaultDisputeGameImpl` (0.8.0), `superPermissionedDisputeGameImpl` (1.0.0), `opcmContainer`, `opcmUtils`, `opcmMigrator`, `opcmStandardValidator` (2.12.0) and `storageSetterImpl` (1.2.2). Earlier releases produced the same extra addresses and also omitted them, so this PR keeps the schema unchanged. Extending `VersionConfig` for the super-root games can be a separate decision.

## Test plan

`go test ./...` in `validation` passes (this decodes both standard-versions files through the Go decoder).

topContributors.summary: oplabs-renovate: Focused on maintaining system integrity by initiating several critical security updates across the infrastructure and optimism repositories. The work involved opening six security-focused pull requests to address vulnerabilities in dependencies such as quic-go (infra#696), brace-expansion (infra#695), and various pion modules (optimism#22181, #22180, #22179, #22178). These efforts highlight a primary focus on proactive dependency management and security patching.

claude: Focused on structuring and expanding the documentation framework for the Optimism ecosystem, notably merging PR #22184 to establish tab skeletons and indices for App Developers and Chain Operators. They also initiated work on the OP Mainnet "keep-and-grow" documentation via PR #22185, contributing over 160 lines of new content and configuration. Their efforts this month were dedicated entirely to improving the information architecture and accessibility of technical docs.

joshklop: Focused on enhancing the reliability of the op-reth node by addressing data consistency during initialization. They initiated work on a significant update to recover proof history gaps on startup (ethereum-optimism/optimism#22177), contributing over 360 lines of new code. This effort included a substantial focus on testing to ensure the robustness of the recovery mechanism. Their primary focus this month was on improving node stability and data integrity within the optimism ecosystem.

sbvegan: Focused on quality assurance and peer feedback this month, contributing two pull request approvals. Their activity centered on reviewing the work of others to ensure code standards were met. Overall, their primary focus was on supporting the development pipeline through the review process.

harshinsecurity: Focused on enhancing the robustness of block processing within the optimism repository, specifically by addressing unhandled payload statuses in the op-node. They authored a significant update in PR #22182 (+94/-4 lines) to ensure the system rejects invalid statuses during the CommitBlock phase. This work involved a balanced effort between core code logic and comprehensive test coverage to validate the new error-handling behavior. Their primary focus this month was on improving the reliability and security of the node's consensus layer through rigorous testing and validation.

antoine-wak: Focused on expanding token availability within the ecosystem by initiating the integration of the WAKU token on the Base network. This effort is represented by an open pull request in ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io (#1345), which involves adding necessary configurations to the platform. Their primary focus this month was centered on ecosystem configuration and asset integration.

NexusAther: Focused on expanding the ecosystem's asset support by initiating the integration of wRATR (Wrapped Ratatoskr) on the Base network. This work is currently captured in an open pull request within the ethereum-optimism.github.io repository (#1346), which involves adding necessary configurations to the platform. Their primary focus this month was centered on infrastructure and configuration updates to support new token listings.

Flotapponnier: Focused on enhancing project documentation by contributing a new benchmark reference for the OP Mainnet RPC. They initiated this work through an open pull request in ethereum-optimism/optimism (#22183), which integrates OpenChainBench data into the existing documentation. Their primary focus this month was exclusively on documentation updates.
